related_questions.question: How long do people live with lung cancer?
related_questions.snippet: The average 5-year survival rate for lung cancer is 18.6%, according to the American Lung Association (ALA). Treatment can help improve lung cancer survival rates and life expectancies. Lung cancer patients can live anywhere from 7-16 months on average, depending on their treatment plan.

related_questions.question: What are the symptoms of stage 1 lung cancer?

text_blocks.snippet: Stage 1 lung cancer often doesn't cause noticeable symptoms, and when they do occur, they can be mild and easily mistaken for other, less serious conditions. If symptoms are present, they may include a persistent cough, shortness of breath, wheezing, coughing up blood, and frequent lung infections according to Verywell Health and the American Cancer Society.
snippet_highlighted_words: persistent cough, shortness of breath, wheezing, coughing up blood, and frequent lung infections

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at potential symptoms:
Early Symptoms (May be subtle or absent):

list.snippet: Persistent cough: A cough that doesn't go away or worsens over time.
Shortness of breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity according to Cooper University Health Care.
Wheezing: A whistling sound when breathing according to Verywell Health.
Coughing up blood or bloody mucus: This is also known as hemoptysis.
Frequent lung infections: Pneumonia or bronchitis that keep returning or don't improve with treatment.
Chest pain: Pain or discomfort in the chest area according to MD Anderson Cancer Center.

text_blocks.snippet: Less Common or More Advanced Symptoms:

list.snippet: Hoarseness: A change in voice according to Cooper University Health Care.
Unexplained weight loss: Losing weight without trying to.
Loss of appetite: Decreased desire to eat.
Fatigue: Feeling unusually tired.
Early detection is crucial: Many lung cancers are found incidentally during routine screenings or imaging for other conditions.
Symptoms can be vague: Lung cancer symptoms can be similar to other, less serious illnesses.
If you experience any of these symptoms, especially if they persist or worsen, consult a doctor for proper diagnosis and treatment: according to Medical News Today.

related_questions.question: Can you be cured of lung cancer?
related_questions.snippet: Some types of lung cancer can be considered cured if diagnosed before they spread, though experts don't often use the word “cured” to describe cancer. More common terms are “remission” or “no evidence of disease” (NED). If you're in remission or NED for five years or more, you might be considered cured.
related_questions.title: Lung Cancer: Types, Stages, Symptoms, Diagnosis & Treatment

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, stage 1 lung cancer is generally curable, particularly when detected early through screenings. The five-year survival rate for stage 1 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is high, ranging from 70% to 92%. Surgery to remove the tumor, sometimes combined with other treatments like radiation therapy, is a common approach, and many patients experience long-term survival after treatment.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, stage 1 lung cancer is generally curable, particularly when detected early through screenings

list.title: Early Detection:
list.snippet: Stage 1 lung cancer is typically localized, meaning it hasn't spread beyond the lung. This early detection is crucial for successful treatment and cure.

list.title: Surgical Removal:
list.snippet: Surgery to remove the tumor is often the primary treatment for stage 1 lung cancer.

list.title: Other Treatments:
list.snippet: Depending on the specific type and characteristics of the cancer, other treatments like radiation therapy, targeted therapy, or immunotherapy may be used in addition to or instead of surgery.

list.title: Survival Rates:
list.snippet: The five-year survival rate for stage 1 NSCLC is significantly higher than for later stages of lung cancer. According to lung cancer information sites, for example, the survival rate is approximately 70-90%.

list.title: Recurrence:
list.snippet: While cure is possible, recurrence is still a concern. It's estimated that lung cancer will recur in 30% to 50% of patients initially treated for stage 1 lung cancer according to Verywell Health.

list.title: Long-term Survival:
list.snippet: Many individuals with stage 1 lung cancer can become long-term survivors with treatment and ongoing monitoring. Some patients may live for 20 years or more after diagnosis.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to consult with a healthcare professional for personalized information about stage 1 lung cancer and its treatment.

text_blocks.snippet: Lung cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the lung. It's a serious condition, with a relatively low 5-year survival rate. Lung cancer is broadly classified into two main types: small cell lung cancer (SCLC) and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). NSCLC is the more common type.
snippet_highlighted_words: a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the lung

list.title: Smoking:
list.snippet: Smoking is the leading cause of lung cancer, responsible for the majority of cases.

list.title: Secondhand smoke:
list.snippet: Exposure to secondhand smoke also increases the risk.

list.title: Radon:
list.snippet: Exposure to radon, a naturally occurring radioactive gas, is another significant risk factor.

list.title: Asbestos:
list.snippet: Occupational exposure to asbestos, a mineral fiber, can also lead to lung cancer.

list.title: Other cancer-causing agents:
list.snippet: Workplace exposure to other cancer-causing agents like arsenic, certain chemicals, and radiation therapy to the lungs can also elevate the risk.

list.title: Genetics:
list.snippet: While not as significant as environmental factors, genetics can play a role in lung cancer development.
Persistent cough: A cough that doesn't go away or worsens over time is a common symptom.
Shortness of breath: Difficulty breathing can be an early sign.
Chest pain: Pain in the chest area, particularly when breathing deeply or coughing, can be a symptom.
Coughing up blood: Hemoptysis, or coughing up blood or rust-colored phlegm, is a concerning symptom.
Unexplained weight loss: Significant weight loss without trying can also be a sign.
Fatigue: Feeling unusually tired or weak can also occur.
Other symptoms: Wheezing, hoarseness, bone pain, headaches, and swelling of the neck and face can also be associated with lung cancer.

list.title: Diagnosis:
list.snippet: Lung cancer is typically diagnosed through imaging tests like chest X-rays and CT scans, followed by biopsies to confirm the presence of cancer cells.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Treatment options vary depending on the type and stage of the cancer, and may include surgery, radiation therapy, chemotherapy, and targeted drug therapies.

list.title: Survival rates:
list.snippet: The average 5-year survival rate for lung cancer is relatively low, around 18.6%, according to the American Lung Association.

list.title: Impact of early detection:
list.snippet: Survival rates are significantly higher for individuals diagnosed with lung cancer at an earlier stage.
